See the whole network

GP

Can assess ADHD and prescribe medication, depending on your state, then keep it reviewed.

  • A diagnosis
  • Medication
  • Reviews

No referral needed.

Psychologist

Talk therapy for ADHD and what comes with it, like anxiety and low mood. Some also assess.

  • Therapy
  • Anxiety and mood
  • Assessment

No referral needed. A GP plan can get you a Medicare rebate.

Psychiatrist

A specialist doctor for complex or overlapping conditions and harder medication questions.

  • Complex care
  • Medication
  • A second opinion

You need a GP referral, which also gets you the Medicare rebate.

ADHD coach

Practical help with routines, planning and getting things done. Most here are former teachers.

  • Routines
  • Study
  • Getting organised

No referral needed. Not covered by Medicare.

Occupational therapist

Routines and strategies for children and teens, built at home, at school or in the clinic.

  • Daily routines
  • School
  • Sensory needs

No referral needed. The NDIS or private health may help with fees.

Counsellor

Counsellors and mental health social workers: someone to talk things through with.

  • Stress
  • Relationships
  • Life changes

No referral needed. Some offer Medicare rebates with a GP plan.

Physiotherapist

Helps you recover from pain or injury and keep moving, at a pace that suits you.

  • Pain
  • Injury
  • Getting active

No referral needed.

Exercise physiologist

Exercise built around you and what you enjoy, for focus, sleep and mood.

  • Movement
  • Sleep
  • Mood

No referral needed.

Therapy assistant

Practises skills with you between sessions, supervised by your psychologist.

  • Practising skills
  • Routines
  • NDIS support

Works alongside your psychologist. Often funded by the NDIS.

Neurotherapy

Brain mapping (QEEG) and neurotherapy sessions, in the clinic.

  • Brain mapping
  • Training sessions

No referral needed. In person only.
